name: Black Buck Ltd
title: Black Buck Ltd - 544288 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Platform growth steady (revenue from ops +42% YoY, adj EBITDA ₹55 cr +16%), but supply-side signals are absent; super loads still in heavy investment phase and fuel recovery uncertain.

summary.headline: BlackBuck Q1 FY27: total income up ~38% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 16% to ₹55 crore, with reported PAT at ₹42 crore after a deferred-tax effect.
summary.overview: Management said the business recovered through late May and June after a weak April caused by macro logistics headwinds. Revenue from operations grew ~42% YoY and ~10% QoQ, while net revenue grew 25% YoY and contribution margin held at ~93%. Adjusted EBITDA rose from ₹47 crore to ₹55 crore, and reported PAT of ₹42 crore fell sequentially from ₹66 crore because of a deferred tax item recognised in Q4 FY26. Growth businesses (Super Loads and vehicle finance) grew ~44% QoQ after ~20% QoQ last quarter.

segments.name: Core businesses (payments/tolling, telematics)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew ~21% YoY and delivered a record quarter for profitability and cash flow. Telematics recorded its highest-ever quarterly new device sales, across AI, non-AI and specialised devices.

segments.name: Super Loads and vehicle finance (growth businesses)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses revenue is up ~2.5x YoY and grew ~44% QoQ, up from ~20% QoQ last quarter. Super Loads now operates in 14 cities. Vehicle finance is expected to reach profitability by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tolling demand has normalised after April; management says it is back to its normal modelling framework (road growth, toll fare inflation, truck growth).
Fuel business is still uncertain. Management gave no timeline for full recovery in fuel loyalty margins.
Super Loads will keep investing aggressively; investment is stepping up each quarter.
Vehicle finance expected to converge to profitability by end of FY27 (reaffirmed).
Effective tax: for the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax; the loss-utilisation view will be reassessed in Q4.
Super Loads segment-level disclosure expected in about three to four quarters, once the business is large enough.
capex_capacity: Super Loads present in 14 cities (4 initial cities plus 10 launched by March/April 2026); live in under 5% of India's industrial hubs.

First Super Loads hub is close to the ~250 loads/day (about 5,000/month) milestone; management says it is about 60-70% there on playbook building, and 70-80% of newer cities are growing faster than the first four.
Telematics device depreciation is front-loaded over two years, which raised depreciation this quarter.
About 40-50% of Super Loads loads are AI-enabled on a given day.
demand_pricing: Tolling GTV grew 16% YoY, which management says is only a low single-digit rise at NETC level and a higher single-digit rise against the CV market.

Renewal rates for telematics: first renewal around 80% for GPS products (early 70s by some accounts), stabilising in the 80s for second and third renewals; higher-end products run 5-10 percentage points better.
Fuelling is a small share of revenue. Management said loyalty margin spend is discretionary and fuel recovery is only partial.
On Delhivery's possible entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance, management sees it as positive for the industry and does not expect near-term threat.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra (Axis Capital): Which hubs is Super Loads present in, daily load volumes, and outlook for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Present in 14 cities; the first four are Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai. Super Loads sequential growth was ~50%, up from ~23-24% a quarter earlier. Detailed volume disclosure is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse (JM Financial): Will the macro headwinds in tolling and fuelling taper in Q2 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling caution has gone away and BAU is restored after a sharp April contraction in normalised swipe metrics. Fuel is only partially recovered, and management gave no timeline for a full recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse: Is Delhivery's entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance a medium-term threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees it as a positive for the industry since there is little qualified competition. It sees no near-term threat and will watch market share closely.

qa_highlights.question: Abhisek Banerjee (ICICI Securities): What drives the 13% growth in transacting users, and what share of users use Super Loads?
qa_highlights.answer: User growth is driven by tolling, telematics and marketplace acquisition, which have been secular for 10-12 quarters. Super Loads is a low-frequency use case and too early to move usage minutes (under 5% of hubs covered).

qa_highlights.question: Monica Joshi: What learnings from earlier cities are being applied to new ones, and how are Bangalore like-for-like numbers trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New cities are layered and run with several parallel experiments; AI-first, less people-dependent workflows are used. Management declined to give like-for-like Bangalore numbers until the segment is large enough to report separately.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: For the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax. The loss-utilisation position will be reassessed at the end of the year (Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

risks_watch: Fuel business recovery: no timeline given, and fuel loyalty spend is discretionary.
Tolling volume: tolling transactions fell 3% QoQ, and tolling GTV growth (16%) lags NETC and the CV market.
Super Loads investment: spending rises each quarter, and segment-level disclosure is not expected for 3-4 quarters.
Reported PAT volatility from deferred tax; the Q4 loss-utilisation reassessment could move reported earnings.
Potential competition from Delhivery in tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on telematics, tolling recovery and Super Loads momentum, but cautious on fuel recovery, with no timeline given. Management deflected granular Super Loads metrics and unit economics, citing limited disclosure.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; down from ₹66 crore in Q4 FY26 due to deferred tax

key_quotes: Despite a very tough April month from a movement perspective, I think there was a decent recovery through end of May and June, which has enabled the business to deliver strong results and something which has helped us get back on track and do well from a BAU perspective.
So, core businesses have again delivered a record quarter from a profitability and cash flows perspective despite the macro headwinds.
We are reaching close to 900,000 transacting customers, and the usage continues to be the same, hovering around 45 minutes daily.
But I don't have a full hold on or let's say to give you a guidance on when will the full recovery sort of you know set in.
So, for the next two quarters, broadly, this trend should continue with deferred tax offsets the tax that is there.
